# Plumber

The reusable workflow scans GitHub Actions on every PR and main push through `tests.yml`, and weekly on its own schedule. The gate requires grade B or better (`soft-fail: false`). `.plumber.yaml` extends the upstream default policy without disabling controls. Its only change adds `softprops/action-gh-release` to the trusted action sources, because `release.yml` creates the GitHub release with it (pinned to a full commit), the same exception `bunkerity/certbot-dns-hosttech` carries.

Every external action is pinned to a full commit. Plumber's binary version is explicit and its SLSA attestation is verified. The job uploads JSON, SARIF, PBOM and CycloneDX evidence as run artifacts. SARIF upload to code scanning is off on pull requests and on private repositories unless `CODEQL_PRIVATE` is `true`, matching the CodeQL availability check. Public score publishing is off on pull requests and private repositories.

The release SBOM uses a version-pinned Trivy binary verified against a fixed SHA-256 before extraction and execution, following BunkerWeb's verified Geckodriver download in `integration-tests.yml`. It does not run an action's downloaded installer. Bump the version and checksum together after verifying the upstream release; no Plumber control is disabled for Trivy.

CodeQL analyzes Python and GitHub Actions workflows and uploads pull request findings to code scanning; its database upload stays off on pull requests. It runs only on a public repository, or on a private one once the repository variable `CODEQL_PRIVATE` is `true` (code scanning on a private repository needs GitHub Code Security). OpenSSF Scorecard runs on public main pushes, weekly and on branch-protection changes. Dependabot groups weekly updates for GitHub Actions, Python development declarations and the capture stack's Docker images. Its weekly pip version scan excludes the generated `requirements-dev.txt`; maintainers regenerate that lock with uv when updating Python tools, preserving AppInspect's transitive constraints. Security-update PRs can bypass the exclusion and require the same lock review.

Local scan results cannot prove hosted permissions, branch protection or public score publishing. Before making this repository public, maintainers must configure main-branch protection, required CI checks, the `release` environment and security features in GitHub. No repository settings are changed by these files.
